prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Pearland, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1295; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident details, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was driving through Pearland on a weekday afternoon, heading south on a two-lane road with a center turn lane. Traffic was light.
Q: What was the speed limit and about how fast were you going?
A: The limit was thirty-five. I'd say I was doing maybe twenty-five, because there was a lot of construction signage.
Q: Tell me what happened next.
A: The other car came over into my lane, I think it was trying to pass a truck in the turn lane. I braked and turned slightly, but we still hit nose to nose. It was a low-speed impact, but I heard the airbags and felt a jolt.
Q: Did either vehicle leave the roadway?
A: No, we both stayed on the pavement. We pulled onto the shoulder after.
Q: Did you get out of the vehicle at the scene?
A: Yes, I walked around for a minute. My neck was already stiff and my lower back started aching within an hour or so.
Q: Have you sought medical care since the accident?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic the same day. They diagnosed a neck and back strain and told me to rest and take anti-inflammatories.
Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?
A: Yes, my neck is sore when I turn my head quickly, and sitting for long periods bothers my lower back. I'm doing some physical therapy exercises at home.
Q: Is there anything else you would like to add about the accident?
A: Just that I was driving carefully and I didn't do anything to cause it. I'd like the claim handled as quickly as possible, since I'm missing some work.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
A: Okay, thank you.
